# Table: a show's data as rows

What a person may set of a table show's data, as the inspector of an episode's Timeline dock shows it (`TableRows` in [src/table/table_rows.gd](../src/table/table_rows.gd)): a field in a table is a row in the inspector, and a key it does not name is shown as what its value is. A track's rows are its law's fields below - each the sentence the puppeteer reads, typed by what the law's sanitizer makes of a track that tells it nothing (`TableRows.law_fields`).

## An act

| Key | In the editor | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | Name | text | What the act is called: what a cue in the words names to start it. |
| `about` | About | text | What the act does, in a few words, for whoever reads the acts. |
| `beat` | Beat | text | The beat it plays in: intro, close, or a beat's number. |
| `length` | Seconds | float | How long the act takes, unless it plays under the words. |
| `under` | Under the words | bool | It lasts as long as the words of its beat, rather than its own seconds. |
| `tracks` | Tracks | data | What it does: each track a law on a thing (and a part of it), as the puppeteer wrote it. |

## A thing on the table

| Key | In the editor | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | Name | text | What the thing is called: how an act and the words find it. |
| `at` | Place (cm) | pair | Where it stands: centimeters right and toward the reader from the middle of the reading. |
| `turn` | Turn (°) | float | Which way its front faces, degrees about the upright. |
| `scale` | Size | float | How large it is against how it was made. |
| `group` | Group | text | The things it belongs with: what stands together, kept apart from other groups. |
| `why` | Why | text | Why it is on the table, as the set dresser said it. |
| `parts` | Parts | data | What it is made of: each part a shape, its size, its material and its place in the thing. |

## A part of a thing

| Key | In the editor | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | Name | text | What the part is called: how a track works it (a jaw, a lid, a wick). |
| `shape` | Shape | enum | What kind of form it is. |
| `material` | Material | ref | What it is made of: one of the table's materials. |
| `size` | Size (cm) | vec3 | Width, height and depth, centimeters. |
| `at` | Place (cm) | vec3 | Where it sits in the thing, centimeters from the thing's middle. |
| `turn` | Turn (°) | vec3 | How it is turned in the thing, degrees about each axis. |

## The laws

What a track may do to its thing (`Motions.LAWS` in [src/table/motions.gd](../src/table/motions.gd)): each law, what it is for, and its fields as the puppeteer is told them.

### `turn` - Turn

it goes on turning (or sliding) at a steady rate - a clock's hands, a turning mobile, a spinning top, a music box's drum, a wheel

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `rate` | degrees a second, counterclockwise as seen from where the hinge's `axis` points - negative turns it clockwise (a slide: centimeters a second); a clock's hands keep its time with `clock` instead |
| `from` | where it starts, degrees from as it was built (left out: where it is) |
| `tick` | steps a whole turn is made in, each a small jump that settles (60 for a ticking second hand; 0 turns smoothly) |

### `clock` - Clock

a clock's hand keeping the video's own time, turning clockwise as seen from where its hinge's `axis` points (point the axis out of the dial's face) - a hand's `runs`, so the clock is never stopped: a wall clock, a pocket watch, a chronometer, a kitchen timer's dial

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `hand` | "hour", "minute" or "second" (a second hand ticks) |
| `shows` | the time "H:MM" the hand points at as it was built (left out: the time it starts at) |
| `time` | the time "H:MM" the clock says as the video starts (left out: what it shows as built) |

### `swing` - Swing

it goes to and fro about where it is - a pendulum, a metronome, a rocking cradle, a balance's beam settling, a glow that breathes

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `amount` | how far each way (degrees, centimeters, or a share for a state) |
| `period` | seconds a whole swing takes |
| `phase` | 0-1, where in its swing it starts |
| `settle` | seconds it takes to die away (0 or left out: it never does) |

### `to` - To

it goes to a new value and stays there - a lid opened, a drink changing color, a heap ground down, a pile rising, a light coming up, a thing appearing

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `value` | where it ends: degrees, centimeters, a share (fill, grow, glow, emit, shown), or a color "#rrggbb" for tint |
| `from` | where it starts (left out: where it is) |
| `between` | [u0, u1]: the stretch of the act it moves in (left out: all of it) |
| `ease` | "both" (slow in and out, the usual), "in", "out" or "none" |

### `path` - Path

it goes through KEYS, on through each one as a hand goes (it stops only at a key it holds or turns back at, and at its last) - a knife's chop, a vial lifted and tipped and set down, a lid lifted and laid aside

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `keys` | [{at (0-1 through the act), value} ...] - or, for a part that moves freely, [{at, by: [x, y, z] centimeters from where it started, turn: [x, y, z] degrees from how it started}, ...]; the first key is where it is at the start |

### `circle` - Circle

it travels round and round a circle, keeping its turn - a spoon stirring, a whisk, a pendulum's bob seen from above

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `around` | the middle: a thing's point ("bowl.middle") or [x, y, z] |
| `lift` | centimeters above the middle |
| `radius` | centimeters, or [across, deep] for an ellipse |
| `period` | seconds a round takes |
| `dir` | 1 clockwise seen from above, -1 against |
| `start` | degrees round where it begins (0 its right, 90 toward the reader) |
| `press` | a thing's name: kept on that thing's surface below it, never through it |

### `aim` - Aim

a held tool posed by TWO of its points, each on its own way - a pestle grinding (its `tip` circling small in the bowl, its `grip` wider above), a whisk, a spoon stirring, a knife rocking on its point

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `tip` | the part's point that leads (by name) and its way: {point, circle or at or path fields} - `{"point": "tip", "around": "bowl.floor", "radius": 1.5, "period": 1.4, "press": "bowl"}` |
| `grip` | its other point and its way, the same |
| `roll` | degrees it is turned about the line between them |

### `carry` - Carry

picked up, carried in an arc and set down somewhere else, turned on the way as a hand would - a jar fetched from the back of the table, a cup taken to the reader's side, a book set on a stack, a thing put back

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `to` | where its middle goes: a thing's point or [x, y, z]; left out, back where it was built - turned as it was built, and a part into its own thing where that thing stands now (a stopper back in its jar, upright) |
| `by` | [x, y, z] centimeters past that |
| `lift` | centimeters it rises on the way (6 is a hand's) |
| `turn` | [x, y, z] degrees it ends turned, from as it was built |
| `between` | [u0, u1]: the stretch of the act it travels in |
| `down` | true: SET DOWN on what is under it - its lowest point comes to rest on the table or on the thing below, however it is turned (a lid laid aside, a spoon put down on its side, a jar stood on a shelf); `to`'s height is then only roughly where |

### `pour` - Pour

a vessel poured into another as a careful hand pours: brought level, its lip held just over the other's mouth and its handle turned away, turned about that lip across the view - so what flows falls where the lip is - slowly until it has emptied, and turned back level; what is in it does the flowing, as much as there is - a jug into a bowl, a ladle into a cup, a flask into a pot, a dish of grains tipped into a jar

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `into` | what it pours into: a thing's or a part's name ("vial 1"), or a point ("bowl.middle") |
| `over` | centimeters its lip is held above that mouth (left out: as low as the mouth's width allows - 1 to 2, a careful pour; more makes a splash) |
| `tip` | degrees it is turned at the most (left out: 120, enough to empty it; less pours only what lies above that) |
| `between` | [u0, u1]: the stretch of the act it pours in - the first third brings it there, the last quarter turns it back |

### `dip` - Dip

a vessel dipped into a liquid and drawn up full, as a careful hand dips: brought over the other's mouth with its handle out over the rim, lowered in tipped only as far as its handle needs to clear the rim, held under while it fills, drawn up slowly so what it cannot hold falls back in, and brought level once it is out - a ladle into a pot, a cup into a basin, a scoop into a cask

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `into` | what holds the liquid: a thing's or a part's name ("pot" is a thing's; "jar/water" a part's) |
| `between` | [u0, u1]: the stretch of the act it dips in - the first quarter brings it there, the last eighth levels it |

### `sprinkle` - Sprinkle

a little of something falls from a point, as grains - a pinch of salt from fingers nobody sees, herbs crumbled off a bundle, seeds shaken from a pod, ash tapped off; they fall, land and heap or sink where they land, as any grains do. (A vessel needs no law to pour: tipped until what is in it reaches its rim, it pours by itself)

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `at` | where it falls from: a point ("bundle.flowers") or [x, y, z] - hold it over what it falls into |
| `material` | a material of the table's (its look, how heavy it is, whether it dissolves) |
| `grain` | a grain's size in centimeters (0.1 a powder, drawn as small clumps, to 1) |
| `amount` | how many grains fall (up to 120) |
| `spread` | how wide it falls, centimeters (left out: 1) |
| `between` | [u0, u1]: when they fall |

### `drink` - Drink

a vessel taken up and drunk from, as a person at the table drinks: lifted toward the lens until it has left the picture by its foot, held there out of sight, and set back exactly where it stood with that much less in it - give it a stretch of at least six seconds, with the words stopped for it, as nobody talks while they drink

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `sip` | the share of what is in it that is drunk (left out: 0.15) |
| `between` | [u0, u1]: the stretch of the act it goes on for - the first third to the mouth, the last third back |

### `assemble` - Assemble

the table's assembly worked, one step after another (ASSEMBLY, below, says what the steps are) - a thing built from many small parts, a part picked up, tried, pressed on or taken off. It takes as long as its steps take, its length worked out from them, and it stretches to fill what its words leave, by stopping between moves, never by slowing them

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `ops` | the steps, in order: each {"do": a step's name, and its fields} |

### `write` - Write

words, a formula or a drawing written onto a sheet (a part of the `sheet` shape) by an unseen pen, stroke by stroke, in a hand - a name on a slip, a label, a line on a page, an equation, a graph; several writes on one sheet go one under another from its head, as lines on a page do, so a page is filled a line at a time (when it is full, write on the next sheet); write only what the script or a card says is written there, or what the work really found

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `text` | the words, a line or a few (\n between lines); math inside them between $...$ in TeX |
| `tex` | in place of `text`: one formula in TeX math, written on its own line - several lines inside \begin{aligned} ... \end{aligned} |
| `draw` | in place of `text`: a drawing, an <svg viewBox="..."> the pen draws (DRAWINGS, below, says what it may hold) |
| `strike` | in place of `text`: the name of an earlier act whose line on this sheet is crossed out - a line drawn through it, for a dead end the work really hit |
| `hand` | neat, quick or print, for words with no math (left out: neat) |
| `with` | the pen that writes it, seen: a thing on the table (or "thing/part"), held by its point `tip` (its nib, else the end of its length) - it is picked up, writes each stroke as the ink goes down, lifts between them, and is held just over the page once the line is done (left out: the pen is unseen) |
| `ink` | "#rrggbb" (left out: a brown-black) |
| `between` | [u0, u1]: the stretch of the act the pen writes in (left out: all of it) |

### `point` - Point

a pen (or any tool held by its tip) brought to something written or drawn on a sheet and held there, its nib just over the paper beside it - sweeping along under a wide formula or curve first - so the viewer sees what is being talked about; start it at the word that names the thing (<!-- act: name -->) and give it as long as the talk about it lasts

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `on` | the sheet it points at, as a write names it ("pad/page 1") |
| `at` | what it points at: a part of a formula written as \pin{name}{...}, an element of a drawing by its id="name", or the name of the act that wrote the line |

### `paint` - Paint

a tool lays elements of a design onto a painted surface, as a careful hand does: fetched from where it rests, loaded from its paint, pressed onto the surface and moved over each element in the way its kind asks - a line drawn along its path in slow strokes, a fill swept back and forth, a fill stippled from its middle out with a sponge, a powder patted on (a little cloud at each pat), dots dabbed, a smear dragged in one pressed stroke, a mist sprayed from a hand's length off, stones carried from their dish and pressed on - lifting between strokes, going back for more when it runs dry, rinsed and dried between colors and before it is put down where there is water for it, and back where it rests at the end. The FIRST act to paint an element lays it; any later one goes over it again with nothing on the tool, softening and smearing its edges (a powder's: sweeping its excess off). It takes as long as its strokes take at a hand's pace, its length worked out from them; slowed, it rests between elements

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `on` | the thing whose surface is painted ("mask", or "thing/part") |
| `paint` | the elements of its design to lay, by id, in the order they go on: ["base"] or ["brow left", "brow right"] |
| `from` | where the tool takes its paint: a pot (a thing, "palette/red" a part, or a point) - for stones, their dish (left out: the paint on the table nearest each element's color) |
| `rinse` | a vessel of water the tool is rinsed in before it takes another color, and when it is done - the water clouds a little with each rinse (left out: never) |
| `dry` | a cloth it is touched to and wiped on after each rinse (left out: never) |
| `manner` | "blend" to go over elements already laid, softening their edges with nothing on the tool; or for a fill, how it is laid - "sweep" (a brush), "stipple" (a sponge), "pat" (a puff) - left out: as the tool is |
| `size` | how wide the tool works, millimeters (left out: as it is built; a tool that presses - a sponge stippling, a puff patting - lays what of it touches, whatever this says) |
